findings.title: Merged PR comment helpers are not on the workflow class
findings.body: get_merged_pr_single_issue_template and _truncate_title were added on the class that owns get_top_5_issues_by_count (the class immediately above OpenPRCommentWorkflow), but the body calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title. GitHubPRCommentWorkflow and GitlabPRCommentWorkflow invoke self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template / self.get_environment_info. Those workflow classes do not inherit this class, and PRCommentWorkflow does not define _truncate_title, so posting a suspect-issue PR/MR comment raises AttributeError and the comment task fails.

findings.title: Issue titles are interpolated into a Markdown link unsanitized
findings.body: MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE wraps the raw issue title in [**{title}**]({url}). Issue titles are attacker-controlled error messages and routinely contain ] (for example foo[0] or KeyError paths). In CommonMark that closes the link label early, so the Sentry bot comment on GitHub/GitLab gets a broken issue link and can be turned into an arbitrary link or extra Markdown. Truncation to 50 characters does not remove ] or newlines. Escape or strip those characters before formatting.

findings.title: Table widget flag renders an empty table instead of query results
findings.body: When organization.features includes use-table-widget-visualization, WidgetCardChart renders TableWidgetVisualization with columns={[]} and tableData hardcoded to data: [] and empty meta. The actual result.data, result.meta, fields, loading state, and custom field renderers are discarded. An empty columns array is also truthy, so the visualization will not fall back to meta.fields. Any org with the flag on sees blank dashboard table widgets.

findings.title: Error payloads are zipped to ids by dict value order
findings.body: fetch_error_details loads nodestore rows with get_multi(node_ids) and then pairs them with zip(error_ids, events.values()). get_multi returns a dict keyed by node id; .values() is not guaranteed to follow error_ids, and omitted missing keys shorten the sequence. The summary can attach the wrong title, message, and timestamp to an error id, or drop errors. Look up each node id explicitly. timestamp is also passed through uncoerced: if the stored event timestamp is an ISO string, error_events.sort and the < comparison in gen_request_data raise TypeError and the summarize request fails.

findings.title: Hidden span attributes are only removed while searching
findings.body: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES (is_segment, project_id, received) is applied only inside the search filter. When searchQuery is empty the function returns the full sorted list, so those fields still render. As soon as the user types a query they disappear, including when the query would otherwise match them. The exclusion needs to run before the empty-search return so the attributes are always hidden.

findings.title: Report time-field validation accepts missing and zero values
findings.body: validate_timestamp and validate_age only run when that field is present, and both use initial_data.get(...) which treats 0 as absent. A report can omit both age and timestamp and still pass, even though the two Reporting API drafts require one of them. A report with timestamp set and age=0 (a valid just-generated report) skips the mutual-exclusion check, so both fields are stored together. The collector then metrics and logs structurally invalid reports instead of returning 422.

findings.title: 60s deadline cannot finish a 100-identity auth refresh batch
findings.body: check_auth marks up to chunk_size (default 100) AuthIdentity rows last_synced=now and then enqueues check_auth_identities. That task now has processing_deadline_duration=60 while each identity does a provider refresh over the network. If the worker kills the task at 60s, the remaining ids in the chunk are not refreshed, and because last_synced was already bumped they will not be selected again until the next ~24h cutoff. Auth sessions that should have been invalidated can stay valid for a day.

findings.title: Trace waterfall container no longer fills its parent height
findings.body: The wrapper that was FlexBox (display:flex, flex-direction:column, flex-grow:1, height:100%) was replaced with Flex direction="column" flex={1}. flex={1} is flex: 1 1 0, not flex-grow: 1, and height: 100% was dropped. The waterfall and its virtualized list size against this container, so the trace view can collapse or stop scrolling to the full viewport height.
